subject: biology
title: Contraception
key_idea: Contraception lowers the chance of pregnancy. Hormonal methods inhibit FSH so no egg matures. (Higher tier) They also inhibit LH so no egg is released. Non-hormonal methods block or kill sperm, or stop an embryo implanting.

blocks.text: Hormonal methods use oestrogen and progesterone, or progesterone alone, to stop eggs maturing or being released.

items: The oral contraceptive (the pill) contains hormones that inhibit FSH production, so no eggs mature.
An injection, implant or skin patch releases progesterone slowly into the blood. It inhibits the maturation and release of eggs for weeks, months or years.
Some intrauterine devices (IUDs or IUSs) release a hormone.
Oestrogen inhibits FSH. With no FSH, the follicle cannot mature, so there is no egg to fertilise.
Progesterone inhibits LH. With no LH, ovulation does not happen.
Progesterone also thickens the mucus at the cervix, so sperm find it harder to reach the egg.
The thickness of the uterus lining changes, so implantation is less likely.
Hormonal contraception inhibits FSH, so eggs do not mature.
(Higher tier) Inhibiting LH prevents ovulation.
Injection, implant and patch release hormone slowly.

blocks.text: Non-hormonal methods stop sperm meeting an egg, or stop an embryo implanting. Sort each method by how it works.

diagram.alt: Sort contraceptive methods by how they work.
diagram.prompt: How does each method prevent pregnancy?

items.text: Abstaining when an egg may be in the oviduct

items: **Barrier methods**, such as condoms and diaphragms, stop sperm reaching an egg.
A **spermicide** kills or disables sperm.
An intrauterine device (IUD) prevents an embryo implanting. It can release copper ions, which thicken mucus so sperm cannot pass, or a hormone, which prevents ovulation.
Abstaining from intercourse when an egg may be in the oviduct means no egg is available to fertilise.
Surgical sterilisation (vasectomy for men, tubal ligation for women) stops sperm or eggs passing.
Barrier methods and spermicides work on the sperm.
An IUD prevents implantation.
Sterilisation is surgical and not easily reversed.

blocks.text: Exam questions ask you to compare methods. Use points for and against, then give a judgement.

rows: Very reliable, easy to take, no need to rely on a partner
Side effects, must be taken every day, no protection from STIs
Lasts about 3 years so no need to remember each day, reversible
Needs a doctor or nurse to fit it, needs replacing after about 3 years, no protection from STIs
Protects from STIs, easy to use, does not affect fertility
Can split, not as effective if past its use-by date, latex allergy, reduced sensitivity
Surgery has risks, such as infection, and it is not easily reversed

Give specific points, such as side effects or no STI protection.
Compare named methods, using any data given.
Finish with a clear judgement linked to your reasons.

blocks.text: Science can show how well a method works. It cannot decide whether it is right to use it, because personal, social and ethical views also matter.

items: Compare reliability, side effects, STI protection and convenience.
Use data and named methods in an evaluation.
Science alone cannot answer the ethical issues.

checks.q: Explain how the contraceptive pill prevents pregnancy.
checks.a: It contains hormones that inhibit FSH, so eggs do not mature. (Higher tier: progesterone also inhibits LH, so ovulation does not happen.)

checks.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of a condom compared with the contraceptive pill.
checks.a: Advantage: it protects against STIs. Disadvantage: it can split, or it can cause a latex allergy.

checks.q: Name two methods of contraception that use hormones.
checks.a: Any two from: the pill (oral contraceptive), injection, implant, skin patch, some IUDs.

exam_phrases: (lack of FSH) so no eggs mature / develop
(lack of LH) so no eggs released or so prevents ovulation
slow release of progesterone / hormone into blood

mistakes.wrong: An advantage of the pill is that you do not get pregnant.
mistakes.right: "You do not get pregnant" is ignored. Give a specific advantage, such as very reliable, easy to take, or no need to rely on a partner.

mistakes.wrong: The contraceptive pill is a barrier that stops sperm reaching the egg.
mistakes.right: The pill contains hormones to stop eggs maturing. A diaphragm is the barrier that prevents sperm reaching the egg. Spermicidal cream kills sperm.

mistakes.wrong: The pill protects against sexually transmitted infections.
mistakes.right: The pill does not protect against STIs. That is a disadvantage compared with a barrier method such as a condom.

worked_example.question: If a man and a woman have sexual intercourse and do not want to produce a baby, they may use contraception. Explain how different methods of contraception prevent pregnancy.
answer_points: The pill, injection, implant or skin patch contain hormones (oestrogen or progesterone) to prevent an egg or follicle maturing, or to prevent ovulation.
A condom prevents sperm reaching the egg, or entering the woman's body.
A diaphragm prevents sperm reaching the egg, womb or oviduct.
An IUD prevents implantation, or releases a hormone or copper ions to prevent ovulation or thicken mucus so sperm cannot pass.
Sterilisation prevents the passage of sperm or egg. With the rhythm method, there is no egg available for fertilisation.
worked_example.tip: Name each method and say how it prevents pregnancy. Link every method to its reason.

exam_phrases: (no FSH means) no eggs will be matured
thickens cervical mucus to prevent the sperm reaching the egg
thins the lining of the uterus so less chance of implanting
stops the sperm and the egg from meeting, so there will be no fertilisation

mistakes.right: Oestrogen inhibits FSH, so the egg or follicle cannot mature. Progesterone inhibits LH (or FSH).

mistakes.wrong: The pill prevents the production of eggs.
mistakes.right: "Prevents production of eggs" is ignored. Say it inhibits FSH or LH, which prevents maturation of a follicle or ovulation.

mistakes.wrong: The pill works because no eggs are released.
mistakes.right: That repeats the question. Say how: oestrogen inhibits FSH so the egg or follicle cannot mature, and progesterone inhibits LH or FSH.

worked_example.question: The combined contraceptive pill contains the hormones oestrogen and progesterone. Explain how high levels of oestrogen and progesterone in the combined contraceptive pill work together to prevent pregnancy.
answer_points: Oestrogen inhibits the production of FSH (1).
FSH causes eggs to mature in the follicle, so with no FSH no eggs are matured (1).
High levels of progesterone inhibit the production of LH (1).
LH causes ovulation, so with no LH ovulation is prevented. If eggs are not matured and released they cannot be fertilised (1).
worked_example.tip: Four linked points score four marks. Thicker cervical mucus preventing sperm reaching the egg can score two.

mistakes.wrong: An IUD is a hormonal method of contraception.
mistakes.right: OCR counts the IUD as non-hormonal. Hormonal and non-hormonal together is allowed, but hormonal on its own is not.

mistakes.wrong: The implant is more successful because it works better.
mistakes.right: Use the data. Fewer women get pregnant with the implant in a year, and it removes user error because you do not have to remember to take a pill.

worked_example.question: Explain how hormones can be used by women for contraception.
answer_points: The treatment contains oestrogen, progesterone, or both (1).
It inhibits LH, which controls ovulation, so ovulation is prevented (up to 2 marks).
It inhibits FSH, which matures eggs, so the egg does not mature (up to 2 marks).
worked_example.tip: Any four points score. Naming the hormone and its effect together can score two marks.
